title: Hex digests derived from a secret rather than from public content
summary: Two hex digests that are computed from a secret rather than from public content: a webhook delivery header X-Hub-Signature-256 (sha256= followed by an HMAC hex digest) and a stored fingerprint field named api_key_sha256 beside a key id.
rationale: A hex digest is not universally benign. An HMAC digest is derived from a shared secret and a payload, so it has the shape of a content hash and a different origin. The provider page defines the header and says to protect the secret, but nothing read says whether the signature value itself is sensitive, and nothing read covers an unkeyed hash of an API key under a field name. Both are ambiguous; neither is bent toward the digest case.
unscopedReason: The values are not issued credentials of a recorded family; the question is whether a derived digest counts as sensitive at all.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted. Missing: a statement that a webhook signature value or an unkeyed hash of a credential is, or is not, sensitive in a log or file. Candidate outcomes: unflagged (the digest cannot recover the secret and is bound to one payload) or flagged under a maintainer policy for replay of one delivery; neither is chosen. The page read defines the header as an HMAC hex digest of the payload with the webhook secret; it says to keep the secret out of repositories, not the signature. Needs a maintainer decision. Downstream: redact-secret owns action policy.

sources.supports: X-Hub-Signature-256 always starts with sha256= and is an HMAC hex digest computed from the payload and the webhook secret token; never hardcode the secret token or push it to a repository.
sources.locator: Validating webhook deliveries; securely storing the secret token

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited pages read on 2026-10-03, before any scanner was consulted. Every value is synthetic: digests are computed over constructed placeholder text, hosts use the reserved .invalid TLD, nothing was tested against any service. No source was found for the stored-hash field; searched the pages above and the OWASP cheat sheets already recorded. Product masking, action policy and measurement stay with the downstream repositories.
